h1:
Eating in Prachuap Town
Noodles, Curry Rice, Breakfast
intro: Prachuap Khiri Khan is a small bayside town that plenty of people drive straight through on the way to Hua Hin or further south. But stop for one meal and you'll find the food here is something locals take seriously — punchy tom yum noodles, late-night rice soup near the train station, southern-style curry rice, and breakfast right by the sea. These are the places people in Prachuap eat themselves.

blocks.html: Prachuap town is small — a few minutes on foot or by car covers most of it. The densest food zone is around Kong Kiat Road and Maharat Road, near the train station and the municipal market. For breakfast and a relaxed coffee, head toward Prachuap Bay, where Khao Chong Krachok hill sits right in front of you. We've picked places locals genuinely go, with the neighborhood and a rough price for each.

blocks.text: The noodles and rice soup locals eat

items.name: Khao Tom Phuean
items.blurb: An old-school late-night rice-soup spot that's a fixture in Prachuap, on Kong Kiat Road near the train station. It opens from evening into the small hours and is where locals meet up after work. Regulars order the tom jap chai (mixed-vegetable stew), crispy pork with kale, and various yum salads, all eaten with hot rice soup.
items.meta: Kong Kiat Road · near the train station · open evening–late

items.name: Tom Yum Noodles 'Ja Kin Ya Bon' (Ta Cha)
items.blurb: A tom yum noodle shop in town that reviewers rave about for loaded bowls and a sharp, sour-spicy broth, with plenty of crispy pork piled on. If you like that tangy, spicy, savory hit, it's worth a stop.
items.meta: Kong Kiat Road · open late morning–afternoon

items.name: Ma Thong Noodles (dry tom yum in banana leaf)
items.blurb: A noodle shop tucked down a side soi. The signature is dry tom yum wrapped in banana leaf, fragrant the moment you unwrap it. They do noodles, rice dishes, and sukiyaki, with low starting prices — good for a light lunch.

items.name: Um's Pork & Tom Yum Noodles (Lan Pa Muay)
items.blurb: Long-running pork and tom yum noodles made from a family recipe passed down through the generations, over near Prachuap Beach School. It's a breakfast-to-lunch spot the neighborhood eats at regularly — mellow, well-balanced broth and house-made fish balls.
items.meta: near Prachuap Beach School · open morning–lunch

items.name: Five-spice duck noodles in town
items.blurb: A five-spice (palo) duck noodle shop that opens around 8am, with soup, dry, and duck-over-rice options. The palo broth is fragrant with spices — a good pick if you want something warm in the morning that isn't rice soup.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: Many shops in Prachuap town take mostly cash, and some close early. Breakfast and lunch noodles often sell out before late afternoon, while rice soup is the late-night option. To eat your way through the list, split it across a breakfast spot and a dinner spot at different places.

blocks.text: Local curry rice and one-plate meals

blocks.html: Prachuap borders the south, so curry rice in town comes in both the central style and the spicier southern style — properly fiery. Local curry-rice shops usually set up early and sell out fast, so go before noon if you want the full spread of dishes.

items.name: Krua Mae Nom Curry Rice
items.blurb: A curry-rice shop in town on Maharat Road, with plenty of dishes to spoon over rice. It's a breakfast-to-lunch spot that local office workers drop by regularly, priced the way a real neighborhood curry-rice place should be.

items.name: Krua Khao Hom Southern Curry Rice
items.blurb: Bold southern-style curry rice with yellow curry, gaeng tai pla, and stir-fried chili dishes to spoon out. If you like proper southern heat, this hits the spot — fiery in the way that goes down easy with hot steamed rice.

items.name: Khao Khayam Pu (a Prachuap specialty)
items.blurb: A dish you'll find at seafood spots in town and along the bay — rice tossed with crab meat and a local seasoning sauce. It's a plate Prachuap takes pride in, and visitors often order it to try alongside seafood dishes.
items.meta: Seafood spots in town / bayside · per shop hours

blocks.html: Breakfast in Prachuap is most fun at the municipal morning market downtown, with savory bites, sweets, and souvenirs to browse. If you want a sea-view breakfast, head out toward Prachuap Bay, where cafes and breakfast stalls look straight out at Khao Chong Krachok hill.

items: Prachuap municipal morning market — a full breakfast spread: grilled pork with sticky rice, pa thong ko (Thai donut sticks), congee, traditional-style coffee, and dried seafood to take home. Easy to graze on as you walk through.

Pa thong ko + traditional coffee — found at stalls in the morning market and old coffee shops in town. Dip them in sangkhaya custard or condensed milk and pair with iced black coffee for an easy local-style breakfast.
Cafes by Prachuap Bay — coffee and a snack with a view of the sea and Khao Chong Krachok in the morning. It's how people in Prachuap like to start the day.
Grilled pork with sticky rice — several morning stalls scattered around town. A breakfast favorite to grab on the go before heading out.

blocks.title: Go early, eat better
blocks.html: The morning market and breakfast stalls are busiest from 6–9am, and the good sweets and dried seafood tend to sell out fast. If you want the full range of souvenirs, getting up a little earlier means more to choose from.

items.name: Seafood by Prachuap Bay
items.blurb: Fresh seafood — sun-dried squid, clams stir-fried with chili paste, sour curry with coconut shoots — eaten in the sea breeze in the evening.

items.name: Late-night rice soup in town
items.blurb: After a night out or a trip to the night market, stop for hot rice soup with small side dishes, local style.

faq.q: What food should you try in Prachuap town?
faq.a: Sharp, sour-spicy tom yum noodles and late-night rice soup are what locals genuinely eat. The standout local specialty is khao khayam pu (crab rice), found at seafood spots in town and along the bay. In the morning, try a plate of bold southern-style curry rice.

faq.q: Where can you get late-night rice soup in Prachuap town?
faq.a: Khao Tom Phuean on Kong Kiat Road near the train station is an old-school spot where locals go for dinner into the small hours. Popular orders are tom jap chai (mixed-vegetable stew), crispy pork with kale, and various yum salads.

faq.q: Where should you go for breakfast in Prachuap town?
faq.a: The municipal morning market downtown has grilled pork with sticky rice, pa thong ko, congee, and traditional coffee. If you want a sea view, head to the cafes by Prachuap Bay that look out at Khao Chong Krachok hill.

faq.q: Do shops in Prachuap town take cards or bank transfer?
faq.a: Local shops and market stalls mostly take cash, though some have PromptPay for transfers. It's best to carry small bills — that's the most convenient.

faq.q: How much time should you set aside for eating in Prachuap town?
faq.a: Breakfast and curry rice are busy from 6–11am and sell out fast, noodles run from late morning into the afternoon, and rice soup is the late-evening option. To eat through it all, split it across a breakfast and a dinner in different neighborhoods.
